content:
I often wind up having to do this too! :) (As it happened, today I derived Repr instances for just about every meta type I could think of to have them on hand for the Meta Café. This amounted to just over 150 deriving instances.)

I think it would be great to just upstream them if possible.

Three tangential things come to mind as pain points when dealing with Repr instances in metaprogramming:

  • It would be nice if deriving handlers could be recursive (moot if all instances exist)
  • It would be nice for the deriving handler for Repr to gracefully create a "stub" view of private fields (e.g. just field := <private>); on some level we want Repr to be usable in source code, but we already abandon this when impractical (e.g. the Repr instance for Name, which displays non-typable .num components)
  • It might be useful to have ReprM for displaying values that need a monad to access, like IO.Refs and lazy data.
Perhaps deriving? for the recursive case (via try this) and deriving! for the fallback?

Something that's a bit annoying about recursive derivation is that it's not always clear what you need to recursively derive. Consider for example

structure Foo where
  x? : Option Baz
  deriving Cls

Perhaps there's a parameterized Cls instance for Option already. Naively, recursive derivation would suggest deriving Cls (Option Baz), but in reality you want to derive a Cls Baz instance.

I remember a discussion we had @Eric Wieser about what if there were a way to get typeclass synthesis to commit to particular choices, especially for error reporting. If synthesizing Cls (Option Baz) could reduce to a "could not synthesize Cls Baz" error, that would help quite a lot for autoderivation.

However, maybe with deriving? this doesn't require quite so much engineering. The way it could work is that it checks if a given type already has an instance (in this example, if we see Option Baz then we see if there's a generic Option _ instance), and if so use that instance to decide which of its parameters likely ought to need instances, then recurse. If it's just for 'try this', then it's ok if it's not perfect.
3 messages were moved here from #lean4 > Adding repr instances in core by Kyle Miller.

Multi-argument deriving instance Cls for T1, T2, T3, ... is a pain point. I think it currently can do any number of things depending on the deriving handler.

I think there's a loose expectation that the types are part of the same mutual block... Maybe the deriving command ought to automatically split these up by mutual block and run the deriving handlers per group. I also don't see why deriving couldn't topologically sort the types, making sure the deriving handlers are run on dependencies first.
